name: Epstein-Barr Virus-associated Carcinoma

criteria.description: Detection of Epstein-Barr virus DNA or RNA in tumor tissue by in situ hybridization or PCR
Histopathological evidence of carcinoma with characteristic morphology consistent with EBV association
Positive immunohistochemical staining for EBV latent membrane proteins (LMP1) or EBV nuclear antigen (EBNA)
Clinical presentation consistent with carcinoma in typical anatomical sites (e.g., nasopharynx, stomach)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of EBV nucleic acid in tumor tissue plus histopathological confirmation of carcinoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of virological, histological, and immunohistochemical findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Common presentation in nasopharyngeal carcinoma subtype
searchTerms: mass in nasopharynx with neck lymph node swelling
nasopharyngeal tumor with enlarged neck nodes
throat mass and swollen neck lymph nodes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Epstein-Barr virus-encoded RNA (EBER) positivity in tumor biopsy
searchTerms: tumor biopsy positive for EBV RNA
EBV RNA presence in cancer cells

common.symptomName: Dysphagia due to oropharyngeal tumor involvement
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing due to throat tumor

common.symptomName: Abdominal discomfort or pain (in gastric carcinoma subtype)

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement
searchTerms: hoarse voice due to nerve involvement

rare.symptomName: Superior vena cava syndrome due to mediastinal mass
searchTerms: swelling from superior vena cava blockage
face and neck swelling from chest mass

laboratory: Elevated EBV viral load in plasma
Positive EBV-encoded RNA (EBER) in situ hybridization in tumor tissue
Elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in advanced disease
imaging: MRI or CT showing mass lesions in nasopharynx or stomach
PET-CT demonstrating hypermetabolic tumor and lymph node involvement
genetic: Presence of EBV genome integrated in tumor cells
Expression of EBV latent genes such as LMP1 and EBNA1
other: Histopathology showing undifferentiated carcinoma with lymphoid stroma
Immunohistochemical positivity for cytokeratins and EBV latent proteins

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of EBV positivity in tumor tissue
Absence of EBV latent membrane protein expression
Negative EBV testing in tumor cells
Lymphoid rather than epithelial tumor origin
Clinical presentation dominated by lymphadenopathy without carcinoma features

references: Young LS, Rickinson AB. Epstein-Barr virus: 40 years on. Nat Rev Cancer. 2004;4(10):757-68.
Tsao SW, Tsang CM, Lo KW. Epstein-Barr virus infection and nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Philos Trans R Soc Lond B Biol Sci. 2017;372(1732):20160270.

Murphy G, Pfeiffer R, Camargo MC, Rabkin CS. Meta-analysis shows that prevalence of Epstein-Barr virus-positive gastric cancer differs based on sex and anatomic location. Gastroenterology. 2009;137(3):824-33.
